Class ChaosFactory

java.lang.Object
com.macstab.chaos.jvm.micronaut.ChaosFactory
@Factory public class ChaosFactory extends Object
Micronaut Factory that exposes the installed ChaosControlPlane as a singleton bean.

The factory is picked up by Micronaut's compile-time dependency injection at application startup. The Requires condition makes the factory back off if the user supplies their own ChaosControlPlane bean (mirroring the @ConditionalOnMissingBean pattern used by the Spring Boot starters).

The returned control plane is the JVM-wide instance; it attaches the agent only when the application's configuration switches chaos on (see chaosControlPlane(Environment)). Closing the control plane is the responsibility of the JVM shutdown sequence; this factory does not register a bean-level preDestroy hook because the chaos platform tolerates multiple close() calls and must remain live for the entire application lifetime.

  • Method Details

    • chaosControlPlane

      @Bean @Singleton @Requires(missingBeans=ChaosControlPlane.class) public ChaosControlPlane chaosControlPlane(io.micronaut.context.env.Environment environment)
      Exposes the JVM's ChaosControlPlane as a Micronaut singleton bean. The agent is attached here only when "macstab.chaos.enabled" is true in the application's configuration and comes from a launch-time local source (see chaosEnabled(Environment)); otherwise the bean is the agent already installed ( -javaagent:, a chaos test extension), and injecting it without one fails. When the attach failed during the context bootstrap (ChaosContextConfigurer logs it and the context starts), creating this bean attaches again and fails with the same error: inject Optional<ChaosControlPlane> or BeanProvider<ChaosControlPlane> where the application must run without the agent.
      Parameters:
      environment - the application's environment
      Returns:
      the JVM-wide control plane
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - when chaos is not enabled and no agent is installed
